column1: # default-way-route.tsv (harbor#1397) — where harbor builds each thing a session would otherwise drop into the box by hand.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Claude Code lets a session write a skill into ~/.claude/skills, a script into ~/.claude/bin,
# a hook into settings.json, a rule into CLAUDE.md or a memory note, and a job into ~/Library/LaunchAgents. Each one
# works until the next deploy overwrites it or leaves it unowned, and nothing said so at the moment it happened.
# default-way-route.sh reads these rows on every Write, Edit and Bash call and, when one matches, names the harbor
# home and the install route. A new kind is a row here, never a change to the script.
# standard_version: 2.0.0
# COLUMNS  kind <TAB> tools <TAB> recogniser <TAB> content <TAB> quiet <TAB> home <TAB> install <TAB> reason
#   kind        the artefact kind, a kebab id; it is the note's subject
#   tools       which calls the row judges, |-separated from Write, Edit and Bash
#   recogniser  cfg:<glob>   a path under the Claude config dir ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.claude)
#               home:<glob>  a path under $HOME
#               cmd:<ERE>    a Bash command segment, split on ; && || | and newlines, heredoc bodies stripped (Bash only)
#               In a glob `*` is one path segment or part of one, and the match also covers everything below it.
#               A Write or Edit is judged by its file_path. A Bash call is judged by what it WRITES: a redirect or
#               tee target, a mkdir or touch operand, or the last operand of cp, mv, ln, rsync, install,
#               ditto, sed -i or perl -i; a directory the glob's last `*` segment sits in counts as a target too. Reads never match.
#   content     an ERE the written text must also match (Write content, Edit new_string, the whole Bash command); - for none
#   quiet       an ERE that, when the Bash command matches it, means the write already goes by harbor's route; - for none
#   home        where harbor builds it, relative to the harbor checkout; {name} is the segment the recogniser's first * matched
#   install     how it reaches the box. `harbor deploy` refuses --apply inside a session and from a worktree, so it is the operator's, from a terminal on merged main
#   reason      one line on why the installed copy is the wrong place
kind
skill
column6: skills/{name}/SKILL.md, with USE WHEN triggers in its description and a row in skills/README.md (a workload's skill goes in its pack's skills/)
column7: harbor skills --apply --live (deploy.sh --only skills); one skill: sh bin/skill-install.sh {name} --apply --live
column8: the skills installer copies tracked skills by byte identity and the catalog indexes what it installed, so a skill written into the box is refused as box-only or overwritten by the next deploy, and no other box or reviewer ever sees it

column1: script
column6: bin/<family>-<object>.sh, its name checked by sh bin/lint-name.sh --check bin <name>, listed in the FILES of bin/deploy-runtime-install.sh, with a row in contracts/cli.md
column8: the runtime installer owns ~/.claude/bin and records each file in .harbor-manifest; a script it did not ship is untracked, untested, and gone or stale after the next deploy

column1: hook-script
column6: hooks/<engine>/<engine>.sh with its manifest.tsv (hooks/README.md); a note or a deny at a tool call is a context rule, context-rules/user/<id>.md with a run: script beside it
column7: harbor deploy --apply --live (the runtime installer copies the engine into bin/, and bin/deploy-hooks.sh wires it from the manifest)
column8: harbor installs nothing into hooks/: an engine runs from bin/ and is wired from its manifest, so a file here is wired by hand, by nobody's registry, and invisible to drift checks

column1: hook-wiring
column6: a wire row in hooks/<engine>/manifest.tsv; for a note or a deny at a tool call, a context rule in context-rules/user/<id>.md, which the injection-rule engine already wired runs
column7: harbor deploy --apply --live (bin/deploy-hooks.sh writes the hooks block from the manifests)
column8: the hooks block is desired state that bin/deploy-hooks.sh writes from the manifests, so a hand-added entry has no manifest row, no controls.tsv row and no off switch anyone can find

column1: constitution
column6: policy/constitution.md; a rule a check can enforce is a context rule (context-rules/user/<id>.md) or a lint, registered in standards/naming/controls.tsv
column8: the box CLAUDE.md is the deployed copy of policy/constitution.md, so an edit here is overwritten by the next deploy and never reviewed

column1: memory-rule
column6: a context rule, context-rules/user/<id>.md (with a run: script when the moment needs a parse), or a lint registered in standards/naming/controls.tsv; keep the note only for what no moment can check
column8: a feedback memory is a rule that reaches a session only when it is recalled; the constitution says a preference that belongs in a config file, a lint or a hook is a missed system patch when it goes into memory

column1: launchd-job
column6: launchd/com.harbor.<family>.<object>.plist, plus its row in docs/reference/checks.md naming what it watches, where it notifies and its off switch
column7: sh bin/deploy-launchd-render.sh launchd/<file>.plist > ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<file>.plist, then launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<file>.plist, from a terminal
column8: a scheduled job with no checks.md row is a check only its author knows about: nobody can trace its alert to it or retire it without reading the source

column1: systemd-job
column6: systemd/harbor-<unit>.service and .timer, the same job as its launchd plist, plus its row in docs/reference/checks.md
column7: cp systemd/harbor-<unit>.service systemd/harbor-<unit>.timer ~/.config/systemd/user/ && systemctl --user enable --now harbor-<unit>.timer, from a terminal
column8: a scheduled job with no checks.md row is a check only its author knows about: nobody can trace its alert to it or retire it without reading the source

column1: cron-job
column6: a launchd plist in launchd/ (macOS) or a systemd user timer in systemd/ (Linux), plus its row in docs/reference/checks.md; harbor schedules nothing with cron
column8: a cron entry is a scheduled job no registry lists: nobody can trace its alert to it or retire it without reading the source
